# FactCheck

> Splits text into claims and checks them against sources. A supported verdict is shown only when a quoted passage or a tool result backs the claim. Opinions are reported as what mainstream fact-checkers say, never as true or false. Strength of support is per claim. There is no overall score. A verdict is not proof.

The check API and MCP plug-in are live.

- Website: https://wellspringwatersolutions-lab.github.io/factcheck/
- API: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com
- MCP: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/mcp

Use the API's own agent instructions first: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/llms.txt

Also available:

- API docs: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/docs
- OpenAPI: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/openapi.json
- Health: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/health
- MCP manifest: https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/.well-known/mcp.json

## Use from an agent

Install the MCP server in Claude or Cursor:

    add https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/mcp to Claude/Cursor

MCP tools: verify_text, verify_claims, get_verification.

Or call the HTTP API:

- POST https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/check
- POST https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/v1/verify

Send JSON with `text` (a passage) or `claims` (a list of strings). You may also send `question`. Set `async` to true to start a background job, then poll GET https://factcheck-mim7.onrender.com/v1/jobs/{job_id} until status is `done`. Fetch a stored result at GET /v1/verification/{id}, or a printable report at GET /v1/verification/{id}/report.

The website form uses POST /check with `{ "text": "...", "async": true }` and no API key.

## Pricing

One free check per client, with no sign-up and no key. Paid plans are coming soon. Paid keys, when they go on sale, will use the Authorization or X-API-Key header. Buying credits is not available yet.

## Verdicts

In this order, from strongest support to least:

- supported
- hypothesis (supported by evidence)
- opinion
- conflicting
- unverified

Do not label an opinion true or false. The API may still return the value `contradicted`; treat that as conflicting.
